records.title: Durable and reversible epigenetic programming of human hematopoietic stem cells as a platform for modulation of platelet function
records.abstract: Programmable epigenome editing offers control of gene expression without altering DNA sequence, but its capacity to program human hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and their differentiated progeny remains incompletely characterized. Here, we establish that DNA methylation-based epigenome editors delivered transiently as RNA induce heritable gene silencing in primary human HSCs. Targeting the platelet integrin β3 (ITGB3) produced silencing that persisted through long-term HSC self-renewal and megakaryocytic differentiation, impaired aggregation of in vitro-derived platelets, and was partially reversed through targeted demethylation at this locus. Silencing remained stable in human HSCs 4 months after transplantation into mice. Targeting additional platelet-associated genes demonstrated broad applicability with this approach. Together, these findings establish DNA methylation-based epigenome editing as a platform for durable and reversible programming of human HSCs and demonstrate its application to modulating platelet function.

Just world belief mitigates depression throughout public health adversity: the immediate and longitudinal mediation of hope
records.abstract: Abstract Belief in a just world (BJW) buffers against negative emotions. According to Lerner’s Just World Theory and Snyder’s hope theory, the buffering effect could be mediated by hope, but empirical evidence is lacking, and the detailed mechanism remains largely unknown. Drawing on the multidimensionality of BJW and hope, the current research proposed a functional specificity model regarding the specific roles of their dual components—namely, agency thinking and pathways thinking (of hope), as well as personal belief in a just world (PBJW) and general belief in a just world (GBJW) in mitigating depression-related symptoms. The model was tested by a cross-sectional design (Study 1, n = 1151) during the COVID-19 lockdown period, as well as a two-wave longitudinal design (Study 2, n = 291) which spanned from 1 month prior to the lifting of the lockdown (Time 1: T1) to 4 months after the lockdown was lifted (Time 2: T2) in China. In Study 1, agency thinking—but not pathways thinking—was found as the primary mediator linking BJW to depression-related symptoms. Notably, PBJW showed a consistent indirect effect via agency thinking (the PAD route), whereas the corresponding effect of GBJW (the GAD route) was weak and unstable. In Study 2, the PAD route remained statistically significant despite the absence of robust lagged effects of agency thinking on depression. The findings provide preliminary evidence that pathways thinking and agency thinking play distinct mediating roles in the influence of GBJW and PBJW on depression-related symptoms. They suggest the necessity of distinguishing between belief systems and motivational processes when examining psychological resilience, particularly in the context of public health crises.

records.title: Spatiotemporal control of CAR-T cell TNF release via tumor-targeted irradiation
records.abstract: Adoptive chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapies have limited efficacy in solid tumors because of poor infiltration and impaired effector function, whereas radiotherapy is constrained by radioresistance and metastatic spread. Here we show that integrating the spatial precision of ionizing radiation with the biological specificity of CAR-T cells enables localized delivery of the inflammatory cytokine tumor necrosis factor (TNF). We identified radiation-responsive genes in tumor-infiltrating T cells and engineered synthetic radioinducible promoters to drive TNF expression. Human CAR-T cells carrying this construct (riTNF CAR-T cells) secreted high levels of TNF upon irradiation, independently of antigen engagement. In human xenograft and murine tumor models, the combination of riTNF CAR-T cells and local irradiation produced greater tumor regression than either treatment alone or standard CAR-T cells with irradiation. This response was associated with high intratumoral, but not systemic, TNF levels, increased tumor necrosis and apoptosis, vascular disruption and greater CAR-T cell infiltration. These findings establish a platform for spatially and temporally controlled cytokine delivery from engineered CAR-T cells.

Creating satisfaction and loyalty among tourists: the power of experiential tourism
records.abstract: Abstract The current research examines whether experiential tourism activities in the tourism industry can influence tourists’ behaviour. Using the stimulus-organism-response framework, the study examines how experience affects travellers’ intentions for satisfaction and loyalty among online travel agents (OTAs). Data were collected from 208 visitors across five travel destinations in India, specifically wildlife sanctuaries and national parks, to examine their lived experiences. The results were analysed using a partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) approach, indicating that experiential tourism indicators have a direct effect on customer engagement. The study suggests that experiential motivation is vital in shaping tourists’ satisfaction and loyalty. The results suggest that tourists are more likely to return to the OTA and recommend it to others if they have positive experiential motivation during their travel encounter. Moreover, the study highlights the importance of co-creation in the tourism industry. In the challenging competitive space, leveraging experiential strategies can help managers gain a competitive advantage. Travel retailers must focus on increasing tourists’ conscious participation and include certain activities that may motivate them and create enthusiasm. This study is one of the few in India to explore the relationship between experiential activities and tourist satisfaction and loyalty among wildlife sanctuaries and national parks travellers.

Single-port Robotic Retroperitoneal Nephroureterectomy with Lower Anterior Access: Surgical Technique, Perioperative and Early Oncological Outcomes from a Multi-institutional Series
records.abstract: Background and objective To describe lower anterior access single-port robotic radical nephroureterectomy (LAA-SP RNU), including bladder cuff excision (BCE) and lymph node dissection (LND), without repositioning or redocking. Methods We present a multicenter retrospective series of 47 patients with upper tract urothelial carcinoma who underwent LAA-SP RNU at five referral centers (May 2024-July 2025). A single 4-cm extraperitoneal incision enabled nephroureterectomy, BCE, and selective hilar/pelvic LND without repositioning or redocking. Data were evaluated using descriptive analyses, and pentafecta achievement for the full cohort was estimated through Kaplan-Meier analysis. Key findings and limitations Median age of the patients was 72 yr; 95% had high-risk disease. LND was performed in 20 patients (43%). Median docking and operative times were 20 and 220 min, respectively; one procedure was converted to open surgery. Grade ≥3 complications occurred in three patients (6%); median hospital stay was 5 d. Pathology showed pT2 and pT3 disease in 15% and 36%, respectively. At median follow-up of 12.3 mo, seven patients (14.9%) experienced recurrence, including five intravesical recurrences; two died from metastatic disease. The 12-mo Kaplan-Meier estimate of pentafecta achievement was 76.7% (95% confidence interval, 62.8-90.5%). This study is limited by potential referral-center and patient-selection bias, heterogeneity in LND and postoperative management, limited follow-up, and the absence of cost-effectiveness data. Conclusions and clinical implications LAA-SP RNU appears feasible and associated with acceptable perioperative and early oncological outcomes in experienced centers. Comparative prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed to establish oncological durability, patient benefit, and cost-effectiveness.

records.title: Predicting chlorination reaction kinetics via a substructure token-based pre-trained model
records.abstract: Prediction of chlorination reaction kinetics is essential for understanding the transformation of organic pollutants during water treatment, but model development is constrained by the limited availability of experimental kinetic data. Here, we developed SPEBERT, a pre-trained chemical language model employing substructure-level tokens, and integrated it with an artificial neural network (ANN) to predict second-order chlorination rate constants (k app ) for 257 organic compounds. Among all evaluated frameworks, SPEBERT-83M-ANN achieved the best performance (R test 2 =0.75, RMSE=1.00, MAE=0.73) and showed better generalization than frameworks without pre-training. Applicability-domain (AD) analyses further showed that prediction performance was associated with both structural and kinetic response coverage of the training set. SHAP analysis identified substructures related to predicted chlorination reactivity and revealed that their SHAP contributions varied with their local bonding environments. Application to 642 river-basin contaminants prioritized seven primary candidates within the AD for subsequent investigation of DBP formation. These results demonstrate the utility of the substructure token-based pre-trained molecular representations for chlorination kinetics prediction under limited data. The framework also provides an interpretable approach for chlorination kinetics prediction and a practical strategy for the prioritization of candidates for subsequent DBP formation investigation.

records.abstract: Cadmium (Cd) phytoextraction often requires balancing metal accumulation with plant growth, yet Cd toxicity constrains photosynthesis and biomass production. Here, we developed a microbiome-guided foliar Bacillus synthetic community (SynCom) for Solanum nigrum, combining Bacillus megaterium NCT-2 with a leaf-derived Bacillus isolate, LE45, selected from the NCT-2-responsive leaf microbiome. SynCom inoculation enhanced leaf colonization, increased leaf fresh weight, Cd concentration, and leaf Cd accumulation by 41.35%, 35.33%, and 91.24%, respectively, and improved magnesium (Mg) accumulation, SPAD and photosynthetic rate. It also reduced chloroplast starch granule accumulation while increasing soluble sugars and amylase activity. Cd partitioning shifted towards cell wall and soluble fractions and away from organelles, accompanied by less labile chemical forms. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses revealed coordinated changes in Mg transport, sugar metabolism, cell wall remodeling, Cd transport and stress-related pathways. Together, these results demonstrate that this simplified two-member SynCom couples Mg-associated photosynthetic activation and carbon remobilization with low-toxicity Cd accumulation, providing a controllable and leaf-centred framework for improving aboveground Cd phytoextraction.

Community health worker-led home blood pressure monitoring in rural sub-Saharan Africa: a diagnostic accuracy study
records.abstract: Background Home blood pressure monitoring (HBPM) coordinated by community health workers (CHWs) is a potential strategy to improve hypertension detection in sub-Saharan Africa, yet data on its diagnostic performance in this setting are scarce. We aimed to determine the diagnostic accuracy of CHW-coordinated HBPM in Kenya and The Gambia using daytime ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) as the reference standard. Methods In this cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study, we recruited a random sample of representative age-stratified individuals aged 30 years or older from the general population of two health and demographic surveillance systems in Kilifi, Kenya, and Kiang West, The Gambia. We used the latest enumeration lists of the two health and demographic surveillance systems as sampling frames and performed computer-generated random sampling within five predefined age strata (30-39 years, 40-49 years, 50-59 years, 60-69 years, and ≥70 years). Pregnant women were excluded, and participants were eligible to participate irrespective of previous hypertension status. CHWs trained and provided participants with HBPM devices for self-measurement of blood pressure twice a day, for a minimum of 3 days and a maximum of 7 days. For the reference standard measurement, an ABPM device was fitted by CHWs, and ambulatory blood pressure was measured every 15 min during the day and 30 min at night. We used blood pressure cutoffs derived from the European Society of Hypertension to determine the age-standardised measures of accuracy (sensitivities, specificities, positive predictive values [PPVs] and negative predictive values [NPVs], positive likelihood ratios [LR+] and negative likelihood ratios [LR-] and area under receiver operating characteristic curves) of HBPM among participants who had valid HBPM and ABPM measurements. Findings Between Aug 18, 2023, and Dec 13, 2024, from 1452 eligible participants, we included 1279 participants with valid HBPM and ABPM measurements (696 in Kenya and 583 in The Gambia). In 1279 participants, the median age was 54 years (IQR 43-66), 805 (62·9%) were women, and 474 (37·1%) were men. The age-standardised prevalence of hypertension on daytime ABPM was 23·1% (95% CI 19·9-26·2) in Kenya and 27·1% (23·6-30·6) in The Gambia while the respective prevalences on HBPM were 32·5% (29·1-35·8) and 31·2% (27·5-34·9). The age-standardised sensitivities and specificities of HBPM were 82·6% (76·2-89·0) and 82·4% (79·0-85·7) in Kenya and 68·7% (61·3-76·1) and 83·5% (79·7-87·2) in The Gambia. The age-standardised PPVs and NPVs were 58·6% (52·0-65·2) and 94·0% (91·6-96·4) in Kenya and 59·9% (52·5-67·2) and 88·1% (84·8-91·4) in The Gambia, respectively. The age-standardised LR+ and LR- were 4·68 (3·67-5·69) and 0·21 (0·13-0·29) in Kenya and 4·15 (3·09-5·21) and 0·37 (0·28-0·46) in The Gambia, respectively. In both countries, the area under receiver operating characteristic curve for HBPM was above 75%. Interpretation HBPM showed moderate-to-high sensitivity and high specificity for detecting hypertension in two rural sub-Saharan African communities. HBPM represents a promising alternative for increasing hypertension awareness in rural sub-Saharan Africa. Facet-dependent As(V) adsorption behavior on goethite: Molecular-scale coordination mechanisms and surface reactivity
records.abstract: Goethite is a major arsenic scavenger in natural waters, sediments, and soils, yet facet-dependent As(V) coordination remains poorly characterized. We studied As(V) adsorption on two well-defined goethite morphologies: plate-like GA (higher (021)/(110) ratio) and rod-like GB (lower (021)/(110) ratio), both dominated by the (110) facet. Results showed GA exhibits a ∼1.5-fold higher As(V) adsorption capacity (5.69 vs. 3.73 µmol/m 2 ) and a ∼3.6-fold higher rate constant than GB (1.34 vs. 0.37 m 2 /(μmol·min). Area-normalized QCM-D revealed ∼1.1-fold faster As(V) deposition on GA, indicating higher loading and faster kinetics on the (021)-enriched GA. At 0.8 mM As(V), pH5.0, in-situ ATR-FTIR, supported by EXAFS and DFT, indicates bidentate inner-sphere complexes dominate on both goethites, with a minor monodentate fraction detectable on GA but not on GB, reflecting different (021)/(110) facet ratios. DFT confirmed the (021) facet has a higher density of singly-coordinated hydroxyl groups and more negative adsorption energies for bidentate and monodentate As(V) complexes (-1.97 to -1.39 eV) than the (110) facet (-1.09 to -0.86 eV), explaining its coordination versatility and higher reactivity. Overall, As(V) adsorption is strongly facet-dependent; enhancing (021) exposure is a promising strategy for tailoring goethite adsorbents, and findings provide a molecular-scale foundation for predicting As(V) mobility in oxic environments.

RSM-optimized ternary Ag-Cu-Zn nanocolloid-based air filters: PM removal efficiency and antibacterial performance compared with ESP/ionizer technologies
records.abstract: Developing air filters that efficiently capture fine particulate matter (PM) while eliminating harmful pathogens without compromising airflow remains a critical challenge in environmental management. To address this limitation, we engineered a scalable, enzyme-free multifunctional nanocolloid-coated fibrous filters (nanofilter) functionalized with a ternary Ag/Cu/Zn nanocolloid coating on polyester (PS) and microfiberglass (FG) substrates. Using response surface methodology and multivariate analysis of variance (ANOVA), the formulation was optimized at concentrations of 807 ppm (Ag), 797 ppm (Cu), and 203 ppm (Zn), with optimized relative nanocolloid application levels of 350% on PS and 400% on FG. The optimized nanofilters exhibited antibacterial performance against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus under UVC-assisted conditions, with no viable colonies detected under the applied experimental conditions. Furthermore, the coated filters improved particulate capture under the evaluated conditions, yielding total mass gains of 4.80 mg (PS) and 10.24 mg (FG) while maintaining low pressure-drop characteristics (<2 Pa at 32 L/min). This ternary Ag/Cu/Zn-based multicomponent platform provides a multifunctional air-cleaning approach by integrating particulate capture with antibacterial activity, offering complementary advantages compared with conventional electrostatic and plasma-based technologies.

Robust fine-mapping in the presence of linkage disequilibrium mismatch
records.abstract: Fine-mapping methods based on summary statistics from genome-wide association studies and linkage disequilibrium (LD) information are widely used to identify potential causal variants. However, LD mismatch between the external LD reference panel and the genome-wide association study population is common and can compromise fine-mapping accuracy. Here we developed Robust SparsePro (RSparsePro), a probabilistic graphical model with an efficient variational inference algorithm, to perform robust fine-mapping in the presence of LD mismatch. In simulation studies with varying degrees of LD mismatch, RSparsePro identified credible sets with consistently higher power and coverage than existing methods. In fine-mapping cis-protein quantitative trait loci and complex trait risk loci, RSparsePro identified credible sets with consistently higher enrichment of variants with potential functional impacts and cross-study and cross-LD-reference-panel replication rates. RSparsePro also identified biologically relevant variants in drug target genes and implicated potential regulatory mechanisms for low-density lipoprotein cholesterol.

records.abstract: High-grade gliomas are the most aggressive brain tumors because of their invasive nature and resilience. Recent advances have shown that glioma cells form synapse-like contacts with neurons, responding to neuronal activity and promoting tumor growth. Glioma-neuron communication is initiated by the release of neurotrophic factors from tumors that exploit host neuronal plasticity mechanisms, subsequently inducing the formation and electrical activity of neuron-glioma synapses. Here, we review the evidence supporting functional neuron-glioma interactions and the molecular regulators underlying neuronal plasticity. Furthermore, we discuss the effects of cancer on neural circuits and the possible prognostic value of connectome studies. Finally, we outline therapeutic strategies and challenges in targeting the neuron-glioma interface to reduce brain cancer progression.

records.title: Biocrusts promote soil multifunctionality recovery in gold mine tailings through heavy metal bioavailability regulation and microbial community reorganization
records.abstract: Biocrusts are among the earliest biological covers established during mine tailings recovery, yet their roles in regulating microbial communities and soil multifunctionality under metal stress are poorly understood. We investigated algal and moss crusts developed along a tailings abandonment chronosequence spanning 4, 6-9, 13, and 30 years in a gold mine tailings pond to analyze their effects on heavy metals, microbial communities, and soil multifunctionality, and identified distinct recovery pathways. Soil multifunctionality was 3.96-9.18-fold higher in biocrusts than in bare sand, with algal and moss crusts showing stronger N- and C-cycling functions, respectively. Heavy metals, particularly Cd, Hg, and Pb, accumulated in biocrusts, whereas bioavailable fractions remained low (0.03%-27.12% of total concentrations), indicating limited metal mobility despite surface enrichment. Biocrusts significantly reshaped microbial community structures, with assembly shifting from stochastic processes during early recovery toward deterministic homogeneous selection at later stages; bioavailable Cd acted as an important environmental filter in moss crusts. PLS-PM revealed that soil multifunctionality in algal crusts was mainly associated with heavy metal accumulation, bioavailability, and microbial richness, whereas moss crusts were linked to soil texture improvement, metal bioavailability, and microbial network complexity. Overall, biocrusts enhance soil multifunctionality through metal availability regulation and microbial network restructuring, providing a sustainable strategy for metal mine tailings restoration.

records.title: Multiscale multimodal integration of spatial omics through a deep generative model with CORAL
records.abstract: Spatial omics enable the in situ characterization of tissue architecture by measuring molecular modalities. However, integrating these datasets remains challenging due to differences in spatial resolution, cross-modal alignment and molecular coverage. Here we show that Cross-scale spatial Omics Registration and Analysis via graph Learning (CORAL), a probabilistic deep generative model, leverages graph attention to integrate diverse spatial transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic and epigenomic data across spatial scales. CORAL jointly models high-resolution datasets with limited molecular coverage and low-resolution genome-wide datasets, generating unified representations with broad molecular coverage and high spatial resolution. Across synthetic and experimental datasets from diverse tissues and platforms, CORAL accurately identifies spatial domains, predicts high-resolution molecular profiles, detects spatially variable genes and infers cell-cell interactions. Applied to spatial transcriptomic and proteomic data from hepatocellular carcinoma patients before and after immunotherapy, CORAL identified organized immune-cell subsets and signaling pathways associated with therapeutic resistance. These results demonstrate CORAL's broad applicability for resolving tissue organization and clinically relevant multicellular interactions.

Response mechanism of forest soil micro-food web to photovoltaic materials exposure
records.abstract: Discarded photovoltaic (PV) materials raise growing environmental concerns, but their impacts on soil micro-food webs remain poorly understood. Here, three commercial PV materials, monocrystalline silicon (MS), polycrystalline silicon (PS), and cadmium telluride (CdTe), were tested in a 30-day soil microcosm experiment. We used energy flow, co-occurrence network, and PLS-PM analyses to quantify effects on soil physicochemical properties, microbial communities, nematode trophic groups, and food web stability. MS exhibited negligible effects under the tested conditions, whereas PS and CdTe significantly altered soil properties, enzyme activities, and microbial composition. PS and CdTe reduced soil micro-food web stability and complexity, shifted energy flow from bacterial to fungal-dominated channels, and suppressed energy transfer to higher trophic levels. Co-occurrence networks revealed that CdTe caused the greatest reduction in network complexity, followed by PS. PLS-PM revealed potential ecological pathways: PS effects were linked to changes in soil pH and environmental conditions, while CdTe effects were associated with Cd release and potential combined Cd-Te toxicity. These pathways are correlative rather than causal, as component-specific controls were not included. Overall, PV materials differ substantially in their ecological impacts, highlighting the need for comprehensive risk assessment and sustainable management strategies for PV waste in terrestrial ecosystems.

Spatial association between atmospheric cadmium deposition and farmland soil cadmium in a karst mining region
records.abstract: Atmospheric Cd deposition supplies ongoing inputs to farmland, but its relationship with soil Cd varies across environmental settings. We examined this relationship using annualized deposition at 78 monitoring sites, 1400 farmland topsoil samples, and enterprise locations in a karst Pb-Zn mining region of southwestern China. Deposition ranged from 0.604 to 21.6 g ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹ . Higher deposition coincided with higher soil Cd around monitoring sites, with rank correlations of 0.278-0.335 after removing broad spatial trends. Spatial-bootstrap intervals for the unadjusted correlations excluded zero at 5 km under both regional partitions, whereas support at 2 and 3 km depended on the partition. Quantile regression using cross-validation-selected deposition estimates and adjustment for soil properties, precipitation, and enterprise density identified a positive association at the conditional 90th percentile of soil Cd (coefficient, 0.604 mg kg⁻¹ per g ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹; Bonferroni-adjusted interval, 0.044-1.237). The Q90 association also remained positive when nearest-enterprise distance replaced enterprise density. These findings show that current atmospheric loading overlaps elevated farmland soil Cd, with the most consistent adjusted evidence in the upper conditional distribution. Joint deposition monitoring and soil surveys can help prioritize investigations of ongoing inputs and farmland contamination.

SOMER: an assessment tool for social acceptance in wetland conservation contexts
records.abstract: Abstract Social acceptance plays an important role in wetland conservation, yet existing studies often rely on context-specific approaches that limit systematic assessment across wetland contexts. To fill this gap, this paper introduces the Social Monitor for Ecosystem Relations (SOMER), an assessment tool designed to examine social acceptance in wetland conservation contexts. In this study, social acceptance is operationalized through individuals’ perceptions of the costs and benefits of wetlands. To demonstrate the empirical applicability of SOMER, the assessment tool was applied in a survey study conducted in the Netherlands (n = 667). We included Nature Connectedness, climate-related perceptions, and contextual factors in this study to explore their associations with social acceptance. The findings indicate that social acceptance is associated with multiple factors, including Nature Connectedness, climate-related perceptions, socio-demographic characteristics, and geographic distance to wetlands. In addition, ecological and recreational dimensions of wetland perceptions were associated with different explanatory factors. By integrating ecological, social, and contextual dimensions, SOMER provides a promising standardized assessment tool for examining the social acceptance of wetland conservation initiatives and supporting more socially responsive environmental planning.

records.abstract: Although poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) show promise for treating homologous recombination-deficient cancers, the observed PARPi hypersensitivity in additional genetic contexts expands their potential use in precision oncology. Yet, the DNA lesions driving PARPi-induced cytotoxicity remain poorly defined. Here we uncover distinct replication-fork lesions in specific genomic regions as key determinants of PARPi cytotoxicity. Using CRISPR screens, we identify that loss of replication-coupled cohesin acetyltransferase ESCO2 confers PARPi hypersensitivity independently of homologous recombination deficiency. Quantitative single-molecule imaging reveals that ESCO2 loss promotes accumulation of G-quadruplex (G4) DNA structures at a subset of replication-associated sites, associated with PARP1 activation and engagement of fork protection factor TIMELESS to mitigate G4-induced stress. Notably, these G4 lesions localize to fragile pericentromeric regions and engage the G4 helicase DDX11. PARP inhibition disrupts this protective G4-processing response by preventing PARP1-dependent engagement of TIMELESS and DDX11, leading to G4 accumulation, DNA damage and chromosomal instability. Together, our findings define the G4-PARP1-TIMELESS-DDX11 axis as a critical safeguard of replication fork stability at hard-to-replicate loci and reveal ESCO2 as a therapeutic target for promoting synthetic lethality in PARPi-treated cancers.

records.abstract: Autonomous sensors and machine learning are transforming ecology by enabling large-scale observation of organisms and ecosystems. However, camera traps, audio recorders and other sensors currently produce species-level detections. Tracking individuals continues to require invasive, high-effort capture-mark-recapture. Here we introduce an automated, general approach that identifies individual animals in passive acoustic recordings based on individually distinctive vocalizations. We train a convolutional neural network to extract salient features from audio recordings using a location-prediction task, then apply dimensionality reduction and clustering on features to achieve song-based individual identification. We identify individuals not included in the training data with 96% accuracy. We apply this approach to track 405 male ovenbirds (Seiurus aurocapilla) from 126 locations across 4 years, then model abundance and apparent survival. We provide open-source code to facilitate applications of our approach to other species. Performing automated individual identification on passive acoustic datasets will support the study of population trajectories and inform proactive ecosystem management to prevent biodiversity loss.

records.abstract: Chemical mixture contamination in complex water samples is typically assessed through toxicity testing of chemically fractionated samples and single compounds or through toxicity-equivalent calculations. However, difficulties in chemical separation and detecting the direct toxicity of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in short-term assays hinder toxicity attribution, limiting the identification of priority PFAS and control areas in highly industrialized watersheds such as the Taihu Basin. To address these limitations, a three-level machine-learning framework based on measured genotoxicity levels was developed to identify PFAS hazards and examine their association with genotoxicity levels and industrial sources. The results demonstrated that short-chain compounds were dominant in the Taihu Basin, and high genotoxicity were detected at the entrances of Taihu Lake. The models suggested associations among short-chain PFAS, industrial emissions and genotoxicity levels. Genotoxicity risk assessments identified PFBA, PFBS, PFOA, and PFOS as priority PFAS. The priority control areas included the Taige Canal, the Wangyu River industrial corridor, and the northwestern entrances of Lake Taihu. The graded warning thresholds were 211.22-83.70 ng/L for total PFAS, 137.05-63.05 ng/L for short-chain PFAS, 54.17-18.55 ng/L for medium-chain PFAS, and 20.00-2.10 ng/L for long-chain PFAS. The three-level interpretable machine-learning framework can quantify the potential contributions of PFAS to genotoxicity.

records.title: Lactylation couples glycolysis with cell cycle progression in cancer cells
records.abstract: Aurora B is essential for mitotic progression, yet whether its activity is regulated by tumour metabolism remains unclear. Here we show that Aurora B functions as a sensor of glycolytic activity and is activated through lactate-dependent signalling. Mechanistically, increased lactate production during aerobic glycolysis promotes KAT2A-mediated lactylation of phosphoglycerate kinase 1 (PGK1) at K131. Lactylated PGK1 phosphorylates Aurora B at T232, leading to cell cycle progression. Disruption of this pathway, either by expressing a PGK1 K131R mutant or a PGK1 variant defective in Aurora B binding, leads to mitotic defects and cGAS-STING activation. These effects suppress tumour cell proliferation and inhibit tumour growth in mice. Furthermore, combining a peptide that disrupts the PGK1-Aurora B interaction with anti-PD-1 therapy enhances CD8 + T-cell infiltration and produces synergistic anti-tumour effects. Collectively, these findings uncover a critical role of glycolysis in governing tumour cell division.

records.abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional virtual histology using synchrotron radiation micro-computed tomography enables non-destructive visualization of biological tissue microarchitecture with isotropic resolution. To support quantitative studies of human pancreatic morphology, we provide high-resolution 3D X-ray imaging datasets of 55 pancreatic tissue cores from 32 individuals. The collection comprises histologically non-diseased pancreatic tissue from organ donors and non-neoplastic regions of surgical resection specimens from patients with pancreatic cancer, including subgroups with insulin-dependent diabetes or following neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue cores with a diameter of 1 mm were imaged at 650 nm isotropic voxel size, yielding a mean effective spatial resolution of 1.66 µm. The cohort includes reconstructed volumes, corresponding immunohistochemistry, clinical metadata, expert-validated annotations, and dataset-specific example 2.5D U-Net models for automated segmentation of islets of Langerhans. A representative co-registered section yielded a Dice similarity coefficient of 0.81 and intersection-over-union of 0.67. This openly accessible, FAIR-compliant resource supports quantitative analysis of endocrine, exocrine, ductal, and stromal architecture and provides a reproducible reference framework for three-dimensional virtual histology of human pancreatic tissue and computational benchmarking.

External validation of an image-only ultrasound model for delivery-date prediction in four Chilean public hospitals
records.abstract: Abstract Pregnancy dating fails the women who need it most: those who reach care without a first-trimester scan. We externally validated a commercial image-only ultrasound deep-learning model for delivery-date prediction, applied unmodified to 64,235 frames from 3788 examinations of 2550 pregnancies (34% migrant) at four Chilean public hospitals. Mean absolute error was 6.9 days versus 11.6 for the conventional due date, yet most of this gain reflected a shorter local gestation and fell below one day against recentred comparators. Fixed-term comparators assign every pregnancy the same gestational age at birth and therefore cannot rank who will deliver early, at any level of point accuracy: accuracy metrics are blind to the ranking on which management turns whenever the outcome distribution is concentrated, as in term-dominated cohorts. In a prespecified landmark analysis the model’s separate image-only risk score discriminated preterm birth with an area under the curve of 0.86, against 0.52 for gestational age alone; outside the landmark restriction it exceeded a clinical baseline of coded diagnoses plus same-examination biometry by 0.09, although it was miscalibrated. Error and calibration were also assessed by maternal nationality. These classification analyses are exploratory, and no woman was managed with the model; they identify what a prospective study should test.

records.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is characterized by chronic inflammation and follicular arrest, yet the molecular drivers linking these pathologies to granulosa cell (GC) death remain elusive. Here, we identify a ferroptosis-inflammation cascade as a critical determinant of ovarian dysfunction in PCOS. We demonstrate that the N⁶-methyladenosine (m⁶A) methyltransferase METTL14 is aberrantly upregulated in human PCOS GCs, correlating with oxidative damage. Mechanistically, we uncover a non-canonical paradigm where upregulated P53 functions as an essential RNA-binding cofactor, recruiting METTL14 to the SLC7A11 transcript. Validated by AlphaFold3 modeling, this METTL14-p53 complex catalyzes SLC7A11 m⁶A hypermethylation and mRNA destabilization. The resulting SLC7A11 deficiency dismantles antioxidant defenses, driving ferroptosis and amplifying local inflammation. Crucially, in a DHEA-induced PCOS rat model, genetic ablation of Tp53 severed this pathogenic axis, restoring redox balance, suppressing inflammation, and reversing the polycystic phenotype. Collectively, our findings reveal a pivotal epigenetic mechanism linking m⁶A reprogramming, iron-dependent cell death, and inflammation, highlighting the METTL14-p53-SLC7A11 axis as a therapeutic target in PCOS.

records.abstract: Although reactive oxygen species promote microplastic weathering, they simultaneously impose detrimental physiological effects on the degrading microbiota. Nanomaterials offer a promising platform for reactive oxygen species modulation and the underlying mechanisms remain largely elusive. This study showed that Pseudomonas sp. JD37, a bacterium capable of producing O 2 •- , removed 65.1% of the organic carbon from solid polylactic acid microplastics (PLA MPs) within 7 days. During this period, the extracellular • OH concentration increased from 0.31 to 1.74 μM. Calcination-derived oxygen-vacancy-rich iron nanomaterials (OV-BFe) increased solid-phase PLA organic carbon removal to 81.7%, while reducing • OH accumulation and alleviating oxidative stress. Mechanistically, OV-BFe reprogrammed NADH/NAD + -dependent phenazine redox cycling and SOD/CAT/POD-mediated reactive oxygen species detoxification, maintaining bacterial redox homeostasis and promoting ester-bond hydrolysis in PLA MPs. This regulation was further supported by dynamic changes in unsaturated and labile metabolites, together with altered expression of genes involved in energy metabolism and oxidative stress- and hydrolysis-related pathways. These findings elucidate the trade-offs between microplastic-induced biostress and microbially mediated microplastic degradation, providing a conceptual framework for improving the bioremediation of biodegradable microplastics.

records.title: Spatiotemporal and process-refined assessment of full-chain toxicity and mitigation potential in China’s mineral phosphate fertilizer production
records.abstract: Sustainable phosphorus fertilizer production relies on the assessment of emitted cadmium (Cd) and arsenic (As), toxicity, and their associated mitigation potential. Existing assessments often employ emissions based on functional units, overlooking the toxicity associated with contaminants that enter the agricultural soils surrounding industrial facilities. In this study, we established a bottom-up assessment model of soil heavy metal(loid)s around industrial enterprises, and applied it to 2247 factories across China. The results indicate that Cd and As emissions during phosphorus fertilizer production in China resulted in a loss of approximately 9370.93 DALY-years of human health damage per million people, which using the normalization index is over 5.3 times that of eutrophication caused by P emissions. This toxicity stems from the use of pyrite and phosphate rock, and diffuses to surrounding soil through surface runoff and atmospheric deposition. The Cd content of phosphate rock is critical for pollution control and can reduce toxicity by 22% at the level of 40-60 mg kg -1 . If advanced phosphorus recovery utilizing sludge and manure as raw material is adopted, the toxicity could be reduced 71% by 2060. These findings provide support for policies regarding short-term pollution control and long-term green transition of phosphate fertilizer production.

records.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 RR) represents a sustainable paradigm for simultaneous environmental remediation and green NH 3 production. While single-atom catalysts (SACs) exhibit immense promise for NO 3 RR, precisely manipulating their localized orbital interactions to decode the underlying structure-activity relationships remains a critical challenge. Herein, using density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we designed a series of interlayer single-metal-atom coordinated porous boron nitride (IC-M/p-BN) acting as efficient electrocatalysts for NO 3 RR. Interlayer metal confinement triggers robust interfacial p-d-p orbital hybridization, establishing an efficient electron relay that empowers surface-exposed non-metallic B sites to act as direct catalytic centers while effectively suppressing the competing HER, NRR and toxic NO/NO 2 byproducts. Crucially, this interfacial charge transfer drives a dynamic B sp 2 -to-sp 3 reconfiguration, facilitating optimal NO 3 - activation. Benefiting from this mechanism, IC-Co/p-BN and IC-Ni/p-BN deliver outstanding NO 3 RR activity (limiting potentials of -0.51 and -0.50 V vs. RHE), significantly outperforming their conventional h-BN counterparts. Furthermore, machine learning analysis identifies the work function as the fundamental descriptor governing NO 3 - adsorption, revealing the interfacial catalytic mechanism. Our work not only offers a robust design strategy for high-efficiency 2D confined SACs but also provides deeper insights into the dynamic NO 3 - -to-NH 3 conversion mechanism at non-metallic interfaces.

records.abstract: Accelerated glacier melt due to climate change is increasingly releasing sequestered antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). However, ARG transmission risk and driven mechanisms that are associated with glacier retreat remain poorly understood. We employed genome-resolved metagenomics along a 246.5 km sampling transect spanning two distinct hydrological seasons and multiple habitats to track the dissemination of ARGs along the hydrological continuum of the Kuoqionggangri Glacier on Tibetan Plateau. Our results demonstrate that hydrological connectivity facilitates the physical transport of antibiotic resistant bacteria. Specific microbial lineages, particularly pathogenic Ralstonia pickettii were traced continuously from glacial sources to downstream rivers, disseminating both ARGs and virulence factors. Beyond host-mediated transport, glacier-derived ARGs can spread into downstream indigenous microbial communities via horizontal gene transfer. Genomic evidence confirmed that sulfonamide and β-lactam determinants transfer across taxonomic boundaries, disseminating from upstream environmental taxa (e.g., Novosphingobium) into downstream opportunistic pathogens. Finally, integrating 156 global glacier metagenomes revealed that the Tibetan Plateau yields an exceptionally high absolute ARG concentration (8.85 ± 0.07 log10 copies/L). Surpassing > 99% of the surveyed regions globally, the sheer magnitude of this genetic discharge identifies glacial melt as a critical emission hotspot, overwhelming downstream aquatic systems with severe ecological resistance risks.

Principles of coarse-scale functional organization in occipitotemporal cortex
records.abstract: Abstract Occipitotemporal cortex (OTC) is known to support visual object processing, yet identifying general principles underlying its coarse-scale functional organization remains challenging. Previously proposed organizational dimensions, such as animacy or real-world size, may not generalize to more diverse, naturalistic stimuli and strong intercorrelations of object properties complicate determining which dimensions, if any, dominate OTC organization. We addressed these challenges through detailed analyses of the cortical topography underlying 15 object properties, using fMRI responses to thousands of natural images, focusing on animacy and size given their established prominence. Our results confirm many characteristics of the purported animacy-size organization, but reveal distinctions that challenge dominant notions of this organization, highlighting the importance of generalizing to large-scale naturalistic data. Beyond animacy and size, many properties could alternatively serve as organizational dimensions, yet none emerges as clearly dominant throughout OTC. Together, our findings reveal a more refined animacy-size organization than previously assumed and highlight challenges of assigning individual principles to account for OTC organization.

records.title: Aptamers enable a distinct mode of conformational DNA recognition
records.abstract: Abstract Watson–Crick base-pairing defines the classical paradigm of nucleic-acid interactions, but growing research reveals noncanonical modes beyond this framework. Here we uncover a mode of interactions by which two DNA strands associate through a ligand-induced conformational rearrangement. Upon binding a small molecule, a structure-switching primary aptamer folds into a conformation that exposes a previously inaccessible docking interface. An independently evolved secondary aptamer recognizes this interface primarily through noncanonical interactions rather than sequence complementarity, reporting the ligand-bound state of the primary aptamer. This interaction is conformation-sensitive: single base-pair changes in the primary aptamer modulate secondary aptamer recognition. Across four chemically distinct small-molecule targets—serotonin, dopamine, testosterone and deoxycorticosterone 21-glucoside—secondary aptamers were identified for three, and the serotonin system was translated into surface-based sandwich assays. These results demonstrate that a ligand-induced conformational state, rather than sequence complementarity or the chemical identity of the ligand, can serve as the epitope for nucleic-acid recognition, expanding the molecular features that DNA can be evolved to detect.

Blinatumomab in dermatomyositis and refractory ANCA-associated vasculitis: a 2-patient exploratory study
records.abstract: Objectives This study aims to explore the safety and efficacy of blinatumomab for the treatment of autoimmune diseases. Methods Two patients, 1 with dermatomyositis (DM) and 1 with antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitis (AAV), were treated with blinatumomab (CD19 × CD3 bispecific T-cell engager antibody) administered by continuous intravenous infusion for 2 cycles. Evaluations were conducted every 2 weeks until week 12, and then once every 4 weeks during continued follow-up through week 24, as well as on week 56. Immune cell dynamics were assessed by flow cytometry and single-cell RNA sequencing. Results During the 14-month follow-up, we observed rapid T-cell activation and B-cell depletion in peripheral blood, together with clinical improvement in both patients, without cytokine release syndrome or other serious adverse events. Moreover, 12 weeks after treatment, both T cells and B cells returned towards a state of homeostasis, accompanied by reduced B-cell activation and downregulation of proinflammatory genes in myeloid compartments. Low-dose blinatumomab treatment was followed by sustained clinical improvement over the 14-month follow-up period, together with marked peripheral B-cell depletion and an acceptable safety and tolerability profile. Conclusions This study provides longitudinal clinical and immunological observations of blinatumomab treatment in anti-Mi-2-positive DM and refractory AAV. These exploratory findings support further evaluation of blinatumomab in autoimmune diseases.

records.title: Efficient and accurate mixed model association tool for single-cell eQTL analysis
records.abstract: Abstract Genetic effects on gene expression often vary across cell types, motivating expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) mapping in single-cell RNA sequencing data. Existing approaches generally aggregate expression across cells, use Gaussian models poorly suited to read counts or do not scale. Here we show that SAIGE-QTL, a Poisson mixed model that directly models single-cell read counts, enables calibrated and computationally scalable eQTL mapping while accounting for donor-level and cell-level covariates and unequal numbers of cells per donor. In simulations and three single-cell datasets, SAIGE-QTL improved statistical efficiency and discovery of genes with significant eQTLs (eGenes) relative to pseudobulk methods and produced results consistent with existing single-cell models at substantially lower computational cost. In 1.2 million immune cells, SAIGE-QTL identified 48.8% more eGenes than pseudobulk analysis. SAIGE-QTL further enabled genome-wide trans -eQTL mapping and rare variant set-based testing, identifying rare variant associations independent of common eQTL signals. SAIGE-QTL therefore expands single-cell eQTL discovery across common, rare and trans -acting genetic variation.

records.title: Soxataltinib, a highly selective CNS-penetrant RET inhibitor demonstrates durable activity in RET fusion–positive non-small cell lung cancer phase 2 study
records.abstract: Selective RET inhibitors have transformed the treatment landscape of RET fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet durable systemic and intracranial disease control remains a major clinical challenge. We conducted a multicenter, single-arm phase 2 study of soxataltinib, a highly selective CNS-penetrant RET inhibitor, in treatment-naïve (n=56) and previously treated patients (n=49) with advanced RET fusion-positive NSCLC. At a median follow-up of 19.3 months, the independent review committee (IRC)-assessed ORR was 84.8% (95% CI, 76.4-91.0), including 89.3% in treatment-naïve and 79.6% in previously treated patients. Responses were observed across clinically relevant subgroups, including patients with baseline brain metastases. Median progression-free survival (PFS) was not reached in the overall population. Intracranial response was observed in patients with measurable CNS disease [ intracranial ORRs were 100% (4/4) in treatment-naïve and 60.0% (3/5) in previously treated patients], supporting clinically meaningful CNS control. Grade ≥3 TRAEs occurred in 76.2% of patients and were generally manageable with dose modification; treatment discontinuation due to adverse events occurred in 1.9%, with no treatment-related deaths. Soxataltinib demonstrated durable systemic and intracranial antitumor activity in RET fusion-positive NSCLC, supporting its further development as a next-generation RET-targeted therapy.

A strongly annotated passive acoustic dataset for tropical bird monitoring
records.abstract: Abstract Passive acoustic monitoring enables continuous, non-invasive biodiversity assessment across diverse ecosystems. The scale of these datasets has driven the adoption of machine learning, with supervised approaches showing strong performance. However, supervised methods require time-resolved annotated datasets, which remain scarce, especially in complex tropical soundscapes. We present PteroSet, a curated dataset of strongly annotated Neotropical bird vocalizations recorded in Puerto Asís (Putumayo) and Pivijay (Magdalena), Colombia, between 2023 and 2025. The dataset comprises 563 recordings (73.62 h) and 15,372 time–frequency annotations, including 6,702 events identified to the species level across 168 species. We release the annotations in a COCO-inspired JSON schema that unifies audio files, taxonomic categories, and labels for machine learning workflows. Beyond providing annotated data, PteroSet serves as a realistic benchmark that highlights key characteristics of tropical soundscapes, including acoustic co-occurrence and domain shift across recording sites. We provide a deep learning baseline for binary bird detection, demonstrating PteroSet’s usability and the challenges it presents.

records.title: The sympathoadrenal contribution to inferior vena cava formation
records.abstract: Abstract Although vascular development is fundamental during embryogenesis, the developmental basis and tissue interactions underlying anatomical variation in major veins are not fully understood. The renal segment of the inferior vena cava exhibits significant anatomical variations that often affect the safety of retroperitoneal surgery. Using mouse embryos, we show that the renal segment of the inferior vena cava is not primarily dependent on the subcardinal vein as classically proposed, but instead forms from a vascular plexus closely associated with the developing para-aortic ridge. Genetic models further indicate that sympathoadrenal development in the para-aortic ridge contributes to the proper organization and remodeling of this vascular network. This revised developmental framework highlights a sympathoadrenal–vascular coupling as a developmental basis for inferior vena cava formation and thereby challenges classical subcardinal vein-dependent models.

Mitochondrial transfer in endothelial cells and vascular health
records.abstract: Mitochondria play a vital role in cellular energy metabolism and vascular health, with their function directly influencing endothelial cell (EC) bioenergetics and integrity. Mitochondrial transfer has emerged as a key mechanism of intercellular communication, impacting angiogenesis, tissue repair, and cellular homeostasis. This review highlights recent findings on mitochondrial transfer, including natural mechanisms - such as tunneling nanotubes (TNTs) and extracellular vesicles (EVs) - and artificial approaches like mitochondrial transplantation. These processes enhance EC function and support vascularization under pathological conditions, including ischemia. While early clinical trials demonstrate therapeutic potential, challenges such as mitochondrial instability and scaling host-derived mitochondria persist. Continued research is essential to optimize mitochondrial transfer and advance its application as a therapeutic strategy for restoring vascular health.

Here, we transform the ancient Wuxing theory into a mechanistically grounded, hypothesis-generating biological framework that conceptualizes cancer cell biology around five mutually interacting processes: Pliability, Hybridity, Aggressivity, Sociability, and Evolutivity (PHASE). By engaging in the circuit of mutual promotion and restriction, these phases form an integrated regulatory system that provides a rationale for organizing diverse malignant properties. records.abstract: Bridging the gap between food production policies and water sustainability requires multi-pollutant perspectives, yet such integrated assessments remain scarce. Here we simulate five food policy pathways (2020-2050) and evaluate their potential to enhance multi-pollutant control in Chinese rivers, explicitly linking the implementation and ambition of food production policies to future water quality. By contrast, ambitious sustainable pathways could reduce most pollutants by up to 41%, primarily through advanced manure and crop management. Controlling microplastic pollution remains a persistent challenge even in our most optimistic pathway, highlighting a critical trade-off with urbanization.

Smoking and Cessation Across the Continuum of Cancer Care: 20 Years of Progress Toward Cessation as Standard Cancer Treatment
records.abstract: In the past 20 years, remarkable progress has been made to address smoking and smoking cessation across the continuum of cancer care. Long-term marketing, misrepresentation, and social engineering led to the substantial rise in smoking and adverse health during the 20th century. Although trends have started to reverse in developed nations in the past 20 years, many low- and middle-income countries have experienced rising tobacco prevalence. Among developed nations, much of the progress in cancer outcomes in the past 20 years can be attributed to reductions in smoking coupled with improved cancer treatments. Alternative products and harm reduction approaches have developed, particularly as related to the rise and use of electronic cigarettes. Continued smoking by patients with cancer and survivors results in continued biological and physiological activities that cause adverse cancer treatment outcomes, including increased overall and cancer-related mortality, risk of second primary cancer, associations with cancer treatment toxicity, and continued risks for non-cancer-related adverse health outcomes. Smoking cessation after a cancer diagnosis is a highly cost-effective adjunct to cancer treatment, resulting in improved survival, improved cancer treatment outcomes, and improved non-cancer health outcomes. Opt-out approaches to smoking cessation have markedly improved reach and overall effectiveness. Addressing smoking as early as possible in the screening, diagnostic, and treatment processes for cancer results in optimal health outcomes and survival benefits comparable to adjuvant cancer treatments. Ignoring or omitting smoking cessation in cancer screening or treatment is in direct opposition to the evidence base and will result in continued harm to patients with associated increased health care costs.

records.title: L-carnitine conjugation: a previously unrecognized pathway proposed for anaerobic benzo(a)pyrene biodegradation by Alicycliphilus sp. T452 under nitrate‑reducing conditions
records.abstract: Anaerobic respiration of microorganisms is a key process driving the degradation of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in contaminated environments. However, the mechanism underlying the anaerobic breakdown of benzo(a)pyrene remains poorly understood, limiting our knowledge of the fate and natural attenuation potential of this hazardous compound. Here, we report a novel nitrate‑reducing bacterium, Alicycliphilus sp. T452, isolated from PAH‑contaminated river sediment, which degrades benzo(a)pyrene under anaerobic conditions with a degradation ratio of 40.6% ± 2.9% over 100 h. Using UHPLC‑QTOF/MS‑based metabolite profiling, 18 potential intermediates were putatively identified, including four L‑carnitine‑conjugated intermediates, of which two were supported by deuterium labeling. Genomic and transcriptomic analyses revealed that specific clusters containing genes encoding Pfam L-carnitine dehydratase bile acid/inducible protein were specifically upregulated during benzo(a)pyrene degradation, providing multi-omics evidence supporting the proposal of a L‑carnitine‑conjugated pathway. This L‑carnitine conjugation likely enhances the solubility and intracellular transport of hydrophobic benzo(a)pyrene‑derived metabolites, representing a proposed microbial strategy to overcome bioavailability constraints. In addition, L‑carnitine is naturally present in anoxic environments, and its conjugation may represent a general microbial adaptation to hydrophobic organic contaminants. Our findings thus expand our understanding of the anaerobic fate of PAHs and offer mechanistic insights into their natural attenuation in contaminated environments.

records.title: Ganaplacide plus lumefantrine solid dispersion formulation for children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria (KALUMI): an open-label, multicentre, randomised, controlled, adaptive, phase 2, non-inferiority trial
records.abstract: Background Ganaplacide plus lumefantrine solid dispersion formulation (SDF) is a novel antimalarial combination shown to be effective and well tolerated in adults, adolescents, and children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria. Here, we aimed to assess food effects on drug exposure and non-inferiority of ganaplacide plus lumefantrine SDF to artemether-lumefantrine. Methods This open-label, multicentre, randomised, controlled, adaptive, phase 2, non-inferiority trial was conducted at ten clinics and hospitals in Burkina Faso, Mali, Côte d'Ivoire, Gabon, and DR Congo. Eligible patients had microscopically confirmed uncomplicated P falciparum malaria. In run-in cohorts 1 and 2, patients (aged 12 years to <18 years with bodyweight ≥35·0 kg) were randomly assigned (1:1) to dosing in the fed group (standard meal 400-500 calories, with 20-30 g of fat) or in the fasted group. Patients received ganaplacide 400 mg plus lumefantrine SDF 240 mg (run-in cohort 1) and ganaplacide 400 mg plus lumefantrine SDF 480 mg (run-in cohort 2) once per day for 2 days. In the main part (cohort 1 [age 2 years to <12 years] and cohort 2 [age 6 months to <2 years]), patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to ganaplacide plus lumefantrine SDF (at the dose regimen selected from run-in cohorts, adjusted by bodyweight) or artemether-lumefantrine for 3 days. Randomisation, using an Interactive response technology system, was stratified by age group and country (cohort 1) or by country (run-in cohorts and cohort 2). Food effects on the bioavailability of ganaplacide and lumefantrine were assessed in run-in cohorts. The primary endpoint for the main part of the study was PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response on day 29 in the per protocol population. The non-inferiority margin was 10%. Safety and tolerability was a secondary endpoint. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04546633 (completed). Findings Between Feb 16, 2021, and July 14, 2024, 577 patients were screened and 282 were ineligible. 51 patients were enrolled in run-in cohort 1, 24 in run-in cohort 2, and 220 in the main part (110 each assigned to ganaplacide plus lumefantrine SDF or artemether-lumefantrine). Two (4%) patients discontinued early in run-in cohort 1 and all 24 in run-in cohort 2 completed the study. Across run-in cohorts 1 and 2, the food effect on ganaplacide was small (mean fed:fasted ratios from 0·98 to 1·41), but a significant food effect was observed for lumefantrine (mean ratios ranging from 1·48 to 2·87). Ganaplacide 400 mg plus lumefantrine SDF 480 mg given once per day for 3 days with a light meal (100-300 calories, with 5-10 g of fat) was selected as the full dose and 206 (94%) of 220 patients completed the main part. For PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response on day 29, response rates were 97 (99% [95% CI 94 to 100]) of 98 in the ganaplacide plus lumefantrine SDF group and 98 (99% [95 to 100]) of 99 in the artemether-lumefantrine group (treatment difference -0·0% [-2·9 to 2·8]), with the lower limit of 95% CI above -10%. We discuss these developments and summarize recent studies defining the role of AR signaling in anticancer immunity. We propose strategies to translate emerging insights into rational trial designs that optimize the integration of AR suppression with immunotherapy.

All preprocessing scripts and the full data-generation workflow are publicly available. Beyond dataset compilation, a convolutional neural network (CNN) was trained for feature extraction and multi-class classification, producing robust descriptor embeddings. Evaluating the effect of a commercial video game on pro-environmental behaviour and its determinants: a pre-post survey study
records.abstract: Abstract Video games reach billions of people worldwide and may offer a scalable opportunity to engage players in climate and environmental action. However, little empirical research has assessed whether video games can influence the pro-environmental behavioural determinants or actions they aim to promote. To address this gap, we evaluated a 21-day ‘green activation’ embedded in Love & Pies, a popular mobile game participating in the 2024 Green Game Jam. The activation encouraged players to adopt pro-environmental behaviours in food consumption, waste management, and habitat restoration through techniques like educational messaging and stories from activists and players. Using a pre–post survey design ( N = 33,910), we assessed players’ self-reported pro-environmental behaviours and key behavioural determinants (e.g. knowledge), linking responses to objective gameplay data. At baseline, players reported moderate levels of subjective knowledge, perceived capability, and outcome efficacy across all three environmental issues. However, one in five players showed low levels of capability and knowledge, suggesting potential targets for intervention. Engagement with the activation, measured by milestones completed, was associated with small increases in subjective knowledge and, to a lesser extent, perceived capability. No consistent associations were observed for other determinants or self-reported behaviours. These findings align with prior research suggesting that games may more readily influence behavioural determinants than actual behaviours. However, video games may be a useful tool for engaging broad audiences with climate issues, particularly when grounded in behavioural theory and designed for repeated exposure to messaging. This study also highlights several design and evaluation challenges in commercial studio environments, as well as future opportunities for collaborative research at the intersection of behavioural science, climate communication, and interactive media.

records.title: A chromosome-level genome assembly of Muscina stabulans Fallén (Diptera: Muscidae)
records.abstract: Abstract Muscina stabulans (Diptera: Muscidae) exhibits a saprophagous–predatory dual-niche life history and is widely used as a forensic indicator. However, the lack of a high-quality reference genome has limited phylogenomics, functional genomics, and the genomic interpretation of forensic traits in this lineage. Here, we present the first chromosome-level reference genome for M. stabulans , generated by integrating PacBio HiFi long reads, Illumina short reads, and Hi-C data. The assembly spans 747.50 Mb (scaffold N50 = 136.70 Mb), with 98.99% of the assembled sequence (739.97 Mb) anchored into five pseudochromosomes. BUSCO analysis (n = 1,367) indicates 97.8% completeness (96.3% single-copy and 1.5% duplicated BUSCOs). High assembly quality is supported by high read-mapping rates, per-pseudochromosome BUSCO completeness, a high LTR Assembly Index (19.86), concordant chromosome-scale coverage, terminal telomeric repeats, and GC content consistency with other muscid genomes. Repetitive elements account for 61.33% of the genome, and we annotated 12,693 protein-coding genes. This chromosome-level genome provides a robust foundation for Muscina spp. genomics and comparative studies across Muscidae.

records.title: Consensus on a core outcome set for ventilation trials in critically ill patients with acute brain injury: results of an international Delphi consensus study
records.abstract: Purpose Clinical research evaluating mechanical ventilation liberation in patients with acute brain injury (ABI) shows substantial outcome heterogeneity, limiting evidence synthesis. We aimed to develop an internationally endorsed core outcome set (COS) and a hierarchical composite endpoint for ventilation trials in neurocritical care. Methods Following COS-STAD/COS-STAP standards, we conducted a 4-round international Delphi study. Candidate outcomes were identified via a scoping review. A multidisciplinary panel from 31 countries scored outcomes using a 9-point GRADE scale. Inclusion required >70% rating as "critical" (score 7-9) and ≤15% as "not important" (1-3). Two consensus meetings were held to categorize outcomes, select representative measures, and ratify a hierarchical composite endpoint. Results 78 stakeholders participated in Round 1; 60 completed all rounds (23.1% attrition). Fifty-four outcomes achieved Delphi consensus. At Consensus Meeting 1, these were organized into 16 categories; the highest-scoring outcome per category was selected. Three outcomes were not ratified due to disease-specificity (NIH Stroke Scale) or lack of universal applicability (brain death, coma-free days). The final COS comprised 13 outcomes across 5 domains: respiratory function, survival, complications, functional status, and quality of life. A 3-level hierarchical composite endpoint was ratified at Consensus Meeting 2: (1) intensive care unit survival, (2) no reintubation within 72 hours, and (3) days alive without mechanical ventilation. Conclusion This study establishes the first COS for ventilation weaning trials in ABI patients. Widespread adoption of these 13 outcomes and the hierarchical composite endpoint will standardize reporting, enable meaningful evidence synthesis, and facilitate clinical translation in neurocritical care. records.abstract: Field-scale remediation of dioxin-contaminated sites conventionally relies on high-temperature thermal technologies requiring secondary incineration above 1000 °C, which entails high energy demand and fugitive emission risks. To address these limitations, we developed a mild-temperature, closed-loop one-pot system integrating solvent washing, in situ sedimentation, UVC photolysis, and solvent recovery. The study comprised two phases: mechanistic evaluation using spiked artificial soil and process validation using field-aged soil with an initial dioxin concentration of 11,776.6 ± 2070.5 pg/g and a toxic equivalency (TEQ) of 537.8 ± 100.9 pg-TEQ/g. In the first phase, methanol-based extraction followed a matrix-controlled mechanism, whereas n-hexane-based extraction was limited by hydrophilic hydration shells surrounding soil particles. To overcome this limitation in the field-aged soil, low-frequency (28 kHz) ultrasound (US)-based process intensification was implemented. At a solid:liquid ratio of 1:10, the integrated process with ultrasonic assistance reduced the final soil TEQ to 131.7 ± 20.4 pg-TEQ/g, below the regulatory threshold of 160 pg-TEQ/g. Under this condition, a subtle toxicity lag was observed, which was likely attributed to the generation of lower-chlorinated toxic intermediates from mass-dominant higher-chlorinated congeners. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the US-assisted one-pot system offers a promising low-temperature alternative to conventional thermal treatment for field-aged dioxin-contaminated soil.

records.title: Seasonal variations and influencing factors of daytime mercury oxidation in the urban atmosphere
records.abstract: Atmospheric mercury oxidation is crucial to global mercury cycling but remains poorly understood, particularly in the complex urban atmosphere. Here we identified the seasonal variations and influencing factors of daytime mercury oxidation in the urban atmosphere using one-year of dual-channel observations, machine learning and chemical box modelling. We found that the daytime increase in GOM/TGM ratio was most pronounced in summer (11.5 ± 5.5%) and weakest in winter (6.8 ± 3.8%). This seasonal variation in mercury oxidation intensity is regulated by distinct factors: oxidation-related species in summer, meteorological conditions in spring and autumn, and particle-related processes in winter. By analyzing the seasonal influence of oxidation-related species, we find that ozone primarily enhances mercury oxidation by promoting the formation of oxidizing radicals, and this promoting effect exhibits clear seasonal variability, leading to the strongest effect in summer and the weakest in winter. In contrast, based on box model results in differentiated scenarios, the NO 2 inhibits mercury oxidation mainly by reducing the availability of oxidizing radicals, and this inhibitory effect shows little seasonal variation. Incorporating the roles of O 3 and NO 2 on mercury oxidation through their seasonally varying regulation of radical availability can provide a more comprehensive understanding of atmospheric mercury oxidation and its cycling patterns.

records.abstract: Plants coordinate defence against pathogens and herbivores through the crosstalk between salicylic acid (SA) and jasmonic acid (JA) signalling pathways. However, little is known about how plants integrate the phytohormone concentration profiles to shape defence states in complex field environments. Here we show that systematically varying combinatorial SA and JA concentrations in Arabidopsis thaliana reveals 43 distinct combination-specific transcriptional signatures beyond SA-JA antagonism. Leveraging these data, we develop and validate machine-learning-based transcriptomic biomarkers that independently measure the SA and JA response states from gene-expression data. Applying these biomarkers to field-grown A. thaliana shows that SA/JA response states are associated with the abundance and co-occurrence patterns of herbivores on individual plants. Our study provides a strategy for decoding hormonal responses to biotic environments from field transcriptomes, bridging the gap between molecular signalling and ecological dynamics.

Advanced translational models and biomarker-guided stratification may help translate these opportunities into more precise therapeutic strategies. In this article, we review these developments and discuss their implications for advanced platinum therapies in TNBC.

records.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics of cellular heterogeneity in Alzheimer disease
records.abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) is defined neuropathologically by the presence of amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles, yet these canonical lesions alone cannot account for its clinical, regional and cellular heterogeneity. AD is a multicellular, spatially organized disease shaped by the interactions of neurons, glia and vascular cells within distinct anatomical microenvironments. Single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing have made it possible to dissect the transcriptional signatures of individual cell populations in the AD brain, revealing selective neuronal vulnerability, stage-dependent glial remodelling and widespread disruption of cell-cell communication networks, whereas spatial transcriptomics and multiplexed imaging have anchored these molecular changes to their tissue context. Studies of defined populations, such as people with autosomal-dominant AD or Down syndrome-associated AD, and of the oldest-old cohorts help disentangle the molecular changes that are causal drivers from those that are downstream consequences. Across individuals, AD heterogeneity is further shaped by sex and ancestry, underscoring the need for broader representation of these factors in single-cell and spatial studies. These advances are also reshaping translational pipelines through multi-omic benchmarking of animal models and single-cell-based drug-repurposing strategies. Thus, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics are redefining our understanding of AD heterogeneity and informing precision approaches to treatment.

However, principled probabilistic frameworks for joint modeling of clonotype and phenotype have remained limited. Here we introduce TCRi, a hierarchical Bayesian information-theoretic framework that infers the joint probability distribution between genetic clonotype and transcriptional phenotype from paired single-cell transcriptomic and TCR sequencing data. TCRi treats phenotype assignment as a probabilistic inference problem: a variational autoencoder embeds single-cell expression into a structured latent space, and a hierarchical Bayesian model learns clonotype-specific phenotype distributions through principled information-sharing across clonotypes, patients and covariates. From these distributions, TCRi computes information-theoretic quantities: clonotypic entropy, phenotypic entropy, phenotypic flux and mutual information between clonotype and phenotype. When TCRi was applied to four real-world datasets comprising 167,118 CD8 T cells from patients with cancer treated with anti-PD-(L)1 immune checkpoint blockade, mutual information emerged as a robust discriminator of therapeutic response.

records.title: Strategic support: lessons learned from staff experiences in UK higher education during the pandemic
records.abstract: Abstract This study examines how institutional support was enacted, interpreted, and evaluated by academic and professional staff in United Kingdom (UK) higher education institutions (HEIs) during the COVID-19 lockdown period (March 2020–August 2021). While universities rapidly introduced wellbeing, mental health, and remote teaching initiatives, less is known about how these measures were experienced in practice and why formally available support did not translate uniformly into perceived support. Drawing on Social Support Theory (SST) as an interpretive framework, this study examines the relational and interpretive mechanisms through which institutional support becomes meaningful, or fails to do so, under crisis conditions. A qualitative-dominant online survey of 290 staff members combined categorical measures of support provision and awareness with open-ended accounts of lived experience. Descriptive analysis mapped patterns of reported provision and line manager engagement, while reflexive thematic analysis explored how staff interpreted and evaluated support initiatives. Findings indicate a consistent distinction between institutional provision and relational enactment. Although many institutions implemented formal support measures, their perceived value depended heavily on personalised leadership practices, including empathy, proactive communication, flexibility, and recognition. Generic or reactive initiatives were frequently interpreted as procedural compliance rather than meaningful care. Differential awareness and accessibility, particularly among part-time staff and employees with disabilities, further revealed how equality-based provision can obscure inequitable experiences of support. By applying SST to inductively generated themes, the study advances understanding of institutional support beyond resource availability, demonstrating that support effectiveness is mediated by relational signalling, contextual sensitivity, and interpretive alignment—that is, the perceived fit between institutional initiatives and staff experience under crisis conditions. The findings refine SST within organisational crisis contexts and highlight the importance of relationally enacted, equity-oriented approaches to support in higher education.

records.abstract: Sympathetic neurons stimulate adipose thermogenic recruitment, which is further sustained by extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling; however, the direct link between sympathetic neurons and ECM remodelling is still missing. Importantly, we identify human GUSB variants leading to the defect of this mechanism, linking this sympathetic-ECM crosstalk to obesity. Furthermore, CS supplementation ameliorates diet-induced obesity by enhancing thermogenic recruitment in murine models. Thus, our findings uncover an ECM-remodelling group of sympathetic neurons important for thermogenic regulation and could serve as a potential strategy against obesity.
