records.abstract: We investigated mouse intraperitoneal acute-toxicity prediction using source-traceable public records, residual diagnostics, and evaluation stratified by structural similarity. Rule-based curation and compound aggregation of TOXRIC and PubChem LD 50 records produced a 34,959-compound development pool and a reserved 1068-compound PubChem-only holdout. The studied 20× OOF discrepancy criterion excluded 448 compounds and retained 34,511 for ECFP4-count/RDKit-2D modeling with multi-seed XGBoost averaging. Database checks reproduced all 448 TOXRIC source values and modeling targets, establishing record traceability without identifying label error. Random and scaffold-based nested evaluations did not show improved R 2 , RMSE, or MAE from exclusion on fixed outer-test populations. The final ensemble achieved a holdout R 2 of 0.7440, RMSE of 0.4703, and MAE of 0.2445 on the -log 10 (LD 50 ,mol/kg) scale. Structural decomposition showed R 2 = 0.9794 for 641 compounds with fingerprint-identical development-set neighbors and R 2 = 0.4290 for the remaining 427 fingerprint-nonidentical compounds. Upstream-record overlap was identified within the fingerprint-identical group. The combined in-domain R 2 of 0.9136 included all 641 fingerprint-identical compounds and 92 similar but nonidentical compounds. These findings distinguish source-record traceability from model agreement and characterize prediction accuracy in relation to structural and provenance support. records.abstract: Tauopathies, such as Alzheimer's disease, are neurodegenerative disorders characterized by the accumulation and propagation of toxic extracellular forms of the microtubule-associated protein tau across brain regions. Microglia, the resident macrophages of the brain, are known for clearing and degrading toxic proteins. However, emerging evidence suggests that microglia also enhance tau spreading. To dissect the molecular mechanisms underlying microglial responses to extracellular tau, we use high-resolution imaging and biochemical approaches to assess the trafficking dynamics of different extracellular tau species in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived microglia. Here we find that tau monomers are internalized by microglia via cell-surface LRP1 receptors but fail to reach terminally degradative lysosomes; instead, they are persistently recycled back to the extracellular space. In contrast, tau fibrils are not internalized and primarily adhere to the cell surface through an HSPG-dependent mechanism, triggering TLR4-mediated microglial activation and the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines. Heparin or anti-tau treatments dampen tau fibril-mediated microglial activation. In addition, disease-associated variants of the Alzheimer's disease-related protein APOE reduce microglia-tau interactions, further reducing tau uptake. Together, these findings demonstrate that microglia fail to efficiently clear extracellular tau monomers and fibrils through mechanistically distinct cellular processes, emphasizing the need for tailored therapeutic strategies to enhance extracellular tau clearance in neurodegenerative diseases.

These changes were also reflected in peripheral blood. Development and validation of early warning scores predicting 24 h mortality addressing intercurrent medical interventions in Denmark: a multicentre retrospective cohort study of 2·08 million hospital encounters
records.abstract: Background The National Early Warning Score (NEWS) is widely used to predict patient deterioration, but retrospective validations face intervention bias and emphasise discrimination performance over clinical utility. We aimed to compare the clinical net benefit of NEWS against simplified scoring rules and machine learning models, to determine whether simpler approaches suffice or if complex models offer meaningful advantages, and to evaluate performance heterogeneity across patient subgroups. Methods In this multicentre retrospective cohort study, we included data from 15 Danish hospitals (ten hospital networks) across the Capital and Zealand regions of Denmark, between Oct 16, 2018, and Oct 16, 2023. We included all adults (aged ≥18 years) with a hospital encounter with at least one NEWS assessment. Demographic and clinical data, NEWS data, and time of death were extracted from hospital and regional electronic health records. Patients were followed up until death or completion of the 24 h observation period after the initial NEWS score was recorded, whichever occurred first. The outcome was all-cause mortality within 24 h of the initial NEWS recording. We compared NEWS against both simpler and more complex approaches for predicting 24 h mortality: simplified NEWS (NEWS without blood pressure and temperature), Demographic Early Warning Score (DEWS; simplified NEWS with age and sex), and a model based on Extreme Gradient Boosting Early Warning Score (XGB-EWS) incorporating vital signs, demographics, laboratory markers, plus medical history embeddings extracted using sentence transformers. We used propensity score weighting to mitigate intervention bias and evaluated performance using net benefit, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, and calibration. Findings This study included data for 2 080 765 hospital encounters representing 825 200 unique patients over 5 years. The majority (50·9%) of the weighted population was aged 18-65 years, 50·4% were female, 49·6% were male, and 66·2% were admitted to internal and acute medicine clinical specialties. Decision curve analysis in the overall population showed maximum net benefit differences of 1·9 additional correct mortality identifications per 10 000 patients between XGB-EWS and NEWS, and 1·5 per 10 000 patients between NEWS and simplified NEWS. However, stratified analyses revealed substantial heterogeneity: in the high-risk group (initial NEWS ≥7), XGB-EWS provided a maximum gain of 78·1 correct identifications per 10 000 patients compared with NEWS, whereas simplified NEWS resulted in a maximum performance loss of 60·2 per 10 000 patients. Conversely, in the low-risk group (NEWS 0-4), differences were minimal: XGB-EWS provided a maximum gain of 0·9 correct identifications per 10 000 patients compared with NEWS, while simplified NEWS resulted in a maximum loss of 0·1 per 10 000 patients. Interpretation Model complexity produced small average clinical utility gains, concentrated among patients initially classified as high risk by NEWS. These findings support prospective trials of risk-stratified monitoring based on the first NEWS assessment, testing simplified approaches for lower-risk patients while retaining full NEWS or electronic health record models for higher-risk patients. Consequently, the coupled system achieves 98.1% PFOA degradation, 68.4% defluorination, stable operation over 120 h of continuous-flow treatment, and favorable techno-economic and life-cycle performance. Mechanistic investigations combined with DFT calculations reveal that deep mineralization originates from the synergistic coupling of enhanced interfacial oxidation power and expanded bulk oxidation opportunity. Quantitative descriptor analysis further demonstrates that PFAS mineralization is jointly governed by oxidation power and oxidation opportunity, rather than either oxidation dimension alone. This work establishes a catalytic framework for overcoming the mineralization bottleneck of persistent contaminants through spatially integrated interfacial and bulk oxidation.

records.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are released throughout production, use, and waste management, leading to persistent environmental contamination. However, comparisons of source-specific profiles, substitution-driven changes, and cross-media redistribution across these stages remain limited. This review synthesizes release characteristics, compositional profiles, and cross-media distribution of low-molecular-weight, non-polymeric PFAS from a life-cycle perspective. Earlier datasets predominantly reported legacy perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids and perfluoroalkane sulfonic acids, whereas later studies documented additional short- and ultrashort-chain PFAS, ether-based alternatives, fluorotelomer-derived substances, and precursors. stems from both improved analytical capabilities and shifts in industrial production and application practices, notably regulatory-driven chemical substitution. Continued releases from products and historical reservoirs (e.g. wastewater treatment plants and landfills), coupled with precursor transformation, maintain the co-occurrence of legacy and alternative PFAS throughout the PFAS life-cycle. These observations indicate that the substitution and treatment may redistribute contamination across compounds, environmental media, and life-cycle stages. However, analytical heterogeneity and limited activity data constrain mass-based source comparisons. Therefore, we propose a source-oriented, mass load-based framework that integrates standardized monitoring, source-specific emission factors, and production, use, and waste-throughput data to prioritize emission sources and distinguish PFAS destruction from cross-media transfer and delayed release.

records.title: Integration and annotation of spatial multi-omic data with DIRAC
records.abstract: Spatial multi-omic technologies measure multiple molecular layers within intact tissues. Two central challenges are vertical integration, which combines different molecular modalities, and horizontal integration, which aligns cell types across studies. Here we show domain invariant representation through adaptive calibration (DIRAC), a geometric deep learning model that unifies these tasks in a generalized domain adaptation framework. DIRAC learns task-discriminative features that are insensitive to domain shifts caused by batch effects, omic modalities or study sites, enabling a shared embedding space and automated cell-type annotation through label transfer from reference datasets. Across sequencing-based and imaging-based datasets, DIRAC identified a new microvascular proliferation domain in glioblastoma, corrected cortical-layer annotations in severe Alzheimer's disease, resolved subtle structures in mouse embryos and remained robust to missing data and unseen cell types. We generated mouse spleen and thymus Stereo-CITE-seq data and used DIRAC to reveal thymic T cell migration and splenic immune cell interactions. DIRAC is fast and scales to millions of cells.

records.abstract: Abstract In China, the rapid spread of digital life has accelerated the growth of online food delivery services. records.abstract: Nitrogen (N) is a key groundwater quality indicator and an important component of biogeochemical cycleing. Existing evidence indicates that elevated manganese (Mn) concentrations in groundwater are closely associated with increases in dissolved organic nitrogen (DON) and ammonium nitrogen (NH 4 + -N). However, the mechanisms by which N influences Mn mobilization in aquifer sediment remain poorly understood. In this study, through microcosm experiments, 16S rRNA analysis, and metagenomic techniques, we elucidated the effects of exogenous DON and NH 4 + -N inputs on dissolved Mn release from aquifer sediments and the underlying microbial mechanisms. At the same N loading, proteinaceous DON induced greater dissolved Mn release than amino acid DON; relative to day 0, dissolved Mn concentrations in the G and B groups increased by 278.5% and 994.7% at day 30, respectively, and this process was mainly associated with microbial processes. In the NH 4 + -N system, dissolved Mn release was likely driven by both biotic and abiotic processes. Relative to day 0, dissolved Mn increased by 70.3% in the N group at day 30, and by 111.9% with AQDS addition at day 30. These findings demonstrate that distinct N-driven Mn mobilization pathways in aquifer sediments, providing mechanistic insights into geogenic Mn release under high-N-loading conditions.

Quartz-rich BBA generated in fluidized-bed combustion is a unique waste stream due to the incorporation of silica bed material; however, its environmental safety and long-term durability constraints remain poorly understood. This study comprehensively evaluated BBAs from industrial-scale circulating and bubbling fluidized-bed biomass power plants to assess their suitability for resource recovery as secondary fine aggregates. Physicochemical characterization (XRF, XRD, SEM-EDS), environmental risk assessment (aqueous leaching, TCLP, BCR sequential extraction, Risk Assessment Code), aggregate performance testing, and accelerated alkali-silica reactivity (ASR) tests were conducted. records.abstract: Background Sabin inactivated poliovirus vaccine (IPV) might be a cost-effective alternative to conventional Salk IPV; however, immunogenicity data for sequential bivalent oral poliovirus vaccine (bOPV)-Sabin IPV schedules used in routine immunisation are scarce. We aim to compare the immunogenicity and safety of Sabin IPV with Salk IPV in routine bOPV-IPV sequential schedules for infants. Methods This single-centre, double-blind, randomised, controlled, non-inferiority trial was conducted at the Siddhi Memorial Hospital (Bhaktapur, Nepal). Healthy infants aged 6-8 weeks, with bodyweight of at least 3·0 kg, and who resided in Bhaktapur without planned migration were eligible. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1), using permuted blocks (sizes two, four, and six), to receive a full dose of Sabin IPV (LG Chem, Seoul, South Korea) or Salk IPV (Bilthoven Biologicals, Bilthoven, Netherlands). Each 0·5 mL dose was given intramuscularly at ages 14 weeks and 9 months. Infants also received bOPV (Bio Farma, Bandung, Indonesia) at ages 6, 10, and 14 weeks as part of routine immunisation. Participants, parents, investigators, clinical and research staff, data analysts, and laboratory assessors were masked to IPV allocation; vaccinators were unmasked. The primary outcome was type 2 seroconversion (change from <8 of reciprocal neutralising antibodies to ≥8 after vaccination) at age 10 months (ie, 4 weeks after the second IPV dose, with a study visit window of 1 week), assessed in the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population as the risk difference with a non-inferiority margin of -10 percentage points. This trial was registered with the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry, ACTRN12622000929707 (completed). The median age of infants was 46 days (IQR 45-48). More male infants (251 [55%] of 459) than female infants (208 [45%]) were enrolled. records.title: Biodegradable cellulose-based composite with tailored wettabilities for highly efficient water-in-oil emulsions separation
records.abstract: The rapid development of the petroleum industry has led to a substantial increase in the discharge of highly stable oil/water emulsions, thereby driving the growing research interest in developing efficient separation technologies for emulsified oil/water mixtures. In line with this, an eco-friendly superhydrophobic cellulose-based composite (RBWC) was fabricated using rice bran wax (RBW) and raw cotton. Upon compression, the material further demonstrated excellent performance toward water-in-oil emulsions. The RBWC exhibited an exceptionally high permeation flux values of up to 13,700 L m -2 h -1 under gravity-driven filtration and 811,000 L m -2 h -1 bar -1 under pressure-assisted filtration for the separation of surfactant-stabilized water-in-oil emulsions. In both filtration modes, the RBWC can achieve excellent separation efficiency with 99.99 wt% oil purity for all the filtrates. On top of that, RBWC possesses good biodegradability, thereby minimizing the risk of secondary contamination after disposal. The excellent separation performance toward various surfactant-stabilized water-in-oil emulsions (SWOEs), together with its recyclability and biodegradability, highlights the potential of RBWC as an excellent candidate for practical applications.

Why and how the humanities matter for sustainability transformations: a humanities-sustainability science bridging perspective
records.abstract: Abstract Hitherto dominant modes of researching and governing transformation(s) are insufficient for society, including science, to adequately respond to the current polycrisis. For science to help guide, steer, and enable transformative change, all disciplines, including the humanities, are needed. The contemporary research landscape on sustainability transformation is diverse yet fragmented. Until very recently, the humanities have mostly occupied a peripheral position within the mainstream transformative change research, in part because their relevance appears less pronounced within positivist and linear frameworks. We aim to reduce this fragmentation by highlighting how concepts and skills from the humanities are applied to research on sustainability transformations. This paper is intended for a diverse readership: sustainability scientists seeking to deepen their transformative impact and humanities scholars looking for interdisciplinary entry points into the discourse on sustainability transformations. We highlight why and how the humanities matter for sustainability transformation by focusing on their contributions to systems, target and transformation knowledge. In particular, we argue that the humanities are uniquely suited to contribute target and transformation knowledge. They support the “how” of transformative change and enable the co-creation of visions and solution options that match the complexity of sustainability challenges. Through nine interrelated points, we illustrate how the humanities are active in co-creating and are further positioned to enrich visions and pathways for sustainability transformation(s).

records.abstract: Antibiotic residues and the environmental dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) pose persistent threats to aquatic ecosystems and public health. A pyrite-based bioelectrochemically enhanced constructed wetland (PBE-CW) was developed to evaluate the removal of enrofloxacin (ENR) and sulfamethoxazole (SMX), responses of resistance-related genetic elements, pyrite interfacial transformation, plant responses, and microbial functional potential. At 1.2 V, ENR and SMX removal efficiencies reached 87.33 ± 3.13% and 99.85 ± 0.32%, respectively. Independent batch experiments showed that applied voltage enhanced ENR and SMX transformation in the pyrite system, accompanied by stronger 1 O 2 signals and multiple intermediates. During long-term operation, pyrite surface oxidation was accompanied by Fe/S dissolution and migration, enrichment of genera associated with electroactivity, Fe/S transformation, and antibiotic degradation, and increased abundances of genes related to extracellular electron transfer (EET), Fe/S cycling, and aromatic compound transformation. Meanwhile, target ARGs and intI1 generally showed lower absolute abundances in the anoxic zone and lower relative abundances in the aerobic zone. Overall, PBE-CW enhanced antibiotic removal and showed potential for modulating resistance-related risks through the integration of pyrite, bioelectrochemical processes, and rhizosphere interactions.

records.title: Evaluation of PainWaive: a consumer-grade EEG headset for remote EEG monitoring and neurofeedback research in chronic pain
records.abstract: Affordable electroencephalography (EEG) headsets could widen access to EEG-based treatment and assessment, but require rigorous validation. We evaluated PainWaive, a custom-developed 2-channel central scalp EEG headset designed for remote EEG monitoring and neurofeedback research in chronic pain. Eighty participants completed two resting-state EEGs using PainWaive and a research-grade system (LiveAmp). Alpha, beta and theta power, and peak alpha frequency (PAF), were derived from homologous central channels. PainWaive demonstrated good-to-excellent test-retest reliability for alpha power and PAF (ICCs = 0.72-0.93), with beta and theta ranging from moderate-good (ICCs = 0.42-0.76). Across 160 home-based neurofeedback sessions in two chronic pain samples, reliability was good-to-excellent across metrics (ICCs = 0.72-0.88). Spectral-shape correlations between PainWaive and LiveAmp were excellent (r > 0.91). Cross-device agreement was moderate-to-good for alpha power and PAF (ICCs = 0.53-0.74), but weaker for beta and theta (ICCs = 0.16-0.51). Sensitivity analyses showed alpha power and PAF were robust across choices, whereas beta and theta agreement varied by pipeline. Overall, PainWaive demonstrated reliable measurement of central scalp EEG metrics, supporting repeated within-device monitoring. Cross-device findings showed correspondence with research-grade EEG for some measures but should not be interpreted as establishing direct numerical interchangeability between systems. These findings provide a technical foundation for future remote EEG and neurofeedback studies in chronic pain.

records.title: A binuclear copper enzyme platform for enantioconvergent radical (pseudo)halogenation
records.abstract: Despite their intriguing native metalloenzymology, naturally occurring copper enzymes remain underexploited for new-to-nature biocatalytic reactions. Here we report the systematic investigation and reprogramming of natural copper enzymes to catalyse unnatural free-radical (pseudo)halogenation reactions with high enantioselectivity. Evaluation of Cu enzymes in the decarboxylative azidation of redox-active esters revealed activity across multiple copper enzyme families, with type III binuclear copper enzymes, particularly Bacillus megaterium tyrosinase (BmTyr), exhibiting superior activity and enantioselectivity towards both stabilized and unstabilized alkyl radicals after further engineering. The strong halide binding affinity of the binuclear copper system also enabled challenging enantioconvergent bromination, chlorination and isothiocyanation reactions that remained inaccessible to repurposed non-haem iron enzymes. Electron paramagnetic resonance and ultraviolet-visible spectroscopic analyses confirmed the coupled binuclear nature of wild-type and engineered bacterial tyrosinases and provided insight into the origin of their enhanced activity. Collectively, this study establishes binuclear copper enzymes as a powerful platform for new-to-nature stereoselective radical reactions, expanding the scope of metalloenzyme catalysis beyond mononuclear systems. The enzyme contains two copper ions each coordinated by three histidine residues. The enzyme acts on a substrate with two chiral centers labeled R superscript L and R superscript S. On the left, the substrate with an azide group (N3) attached to the R superscript S center is shown as a reactant. On the right, the product has a substituent labeled X, which can be chlorine, bromine, or thiocyanate, attached to the R superscript S center. records.title: Combination antiviral treatment for a patient with lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus meningoencephalitis associated with bispecific antibody teclistamab therapy for myeloma
records.abstract: Lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) is a rare cause of meningoencephalitis in humans. Although LCMV is a rodent zoonosis with a global distribution, no UK cases in humans have been reported in published literature since the 1950s, and testing is rarely performed. LCMV meningoencephalitis is self-limiting in people who are immunocompetent, but infection in hosts who are immunocompromised causes severe disease. We report a presentation of LCMV meningoencephalitis in a patient with relapsed multiple myeloma receiving teclistamab. The patient presented with a 5-month history of progressive neurological symptoms, including hearing loss, ataxia, headache, and weight loss. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis showed lymphocytic pleocytosis, markedly elevated protein concentration, and hypoglycorrhachia. Extensive microbiological and autoimmune investigations were negative, and empirical antimicrobial and antituberculosis therapies did not prevent clinical deterioration. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing of CSF identified LCMV, and a history of domestic rodent exposure was subsequently identified. Combination antiviral therapy with ribavirin, remdesivir, and molnupiravir was initiated. Molnupiravir was later substituted for favipiravir, and favipiravir dosing was guided by serum and CSF therapeutic drug monitoring. The patient showed sustained neurological improvement, with clearance of LCMV from CSF and blood within 2 months. Antiviral therapy continued for 6 months. The patient regained functional independence and returned to work, with only mild residual symptoms. In addition to reporting a novel occurrence of LCMV infection in a patient on teclistamab, the case highlights the presence of LCMV in the UK and the utility of metagenomic next-generation sequencing for pathogen identification in undiagnosed encephalitis. Finally, the case provides preliminary evidence supporting combination antiviral therapy in persistent LCMV infection.

records.title: Plant sexual reproduction in a warming world
records.abstract: Sexual reproduction is the most heat-sensitive phase of the plant life cycle; however, studies of reproductive failure under heat stress have primarily focused on individual organs. Here, we propose a conceptual framework in which heat stress causes a system-level breakdown of male and female gametophyte development, shared metabolic and proteostatic support networks, and pollen-pistil interaction. This combined collapse within a narrow temperature window cannot be predicted from individual organs or gametophytes. Heat also remodels epigenetic makeup, generating stress memory, though its transmission across generations remains unresolved. We highlight that techniques such as single-cell omics, AI-driven phenotyping, and genome editing can provide valuable mechanistic insights to support the development of predictive, actionable breeding strategies for heat-resilient crops.

The carbon at risk measure for managing carbon removal risk and guiding portfolio construction
records.abstract: Abstract Carbon removal markets lack a standardized, quantitative measure of permanence risk. Inspired by value at risk in financial markets, we propose carbon at risk (CaR): a probabilistic measure of the shortfall between contracted removals and realized storage at a given confidence level and time horizon. We calibrate CaR in two proof-of-concept applications: forest carbon, where Monte Carlo simulations driven by satellite fire data yield a single-project 95% CaR of more than 70% over 200 years for California, and geological storage, where simulations using the Storage Security Calculator show that the 95% CaR ranges from 0.15% (well-regulated offshore) to 17% (poorly regulated onshore). Combining technologies in a portfolio can help manage tail risk cost-effectively. The minimum cost of meeting a permanence target depends on the magnitude and correlation structure of key risk factors. CaR provides a technology-agnostic basis for risk-calibrated buffer sizing, insurance pricing and reserve-fund design, over both policy- and climate-relevant horizons.

records.title: MambaSleepCVD for prediction of long term cardiovascular outcomes from polysomnography
records.abstract: Abstract Long-term cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk prediction remains a major global clinical priority. This study investigates how much prognostic information full-night polysomnography (PSG) carries after explicitly controlling demographic confounding, and whether combining specialized unimodal representations with continuous fusion mechanisms can effectively leverage it. We adopt a modular framework based on Coupled Mamba for simultaneous cross-modal and temporal fusion, capturing long-range dependencies and dynamic interactions between physiological modalities throughout sleep. With this capability, we assess whether specialized supervised representations from task-specific unimodal encoders offer prognostic value comparable to task-agnostic multimodal self-supervised pre-training. Validated on the Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS) dataset, our approach achieves performance comparable to or better than current state-of-the-art architectures in the fully supervised, data-abundant regime, although the cardiac channel alone accounts for most of the discriminative signal. More importantly, we show that in the reference dataset chronological age strongly drives survival ranking; when provided as an explicit input, it can create a shortcut that obscures the contribution of PSG-derived physiology. Ultimately, our findings suggest that supervised unimodal experts integrated through a fusion engine provide a flexible pathway for prognostic risk ranking from sleep recordings, while reliable CVD screening will require independent external cohorts and explicit confounder control.

records.abstract: Advances in single-cell sequencing and spatial omics technologies have enhanced our understanding of diverse cellular identities, compositions, architectures and functions. new_candidate_reviews.title: Predicting chlorination reaction kinetics via a substructure token-based pre-trained model
new_candidate_reviews.abstract: Prediction of chlorination reaction kinetics is essential for understanding the transformation of organic pollutants during water treatment, but model development is constrained by the limited availability of experimental kinetic data. Among all evaluated frameworks, SPEBERT-83M-ANN achieved the best performance (R test 2 =0.75, RMSE=1.00, MAE=0.73) and showed better generalization than frameworks without pre-training. Applicability-domain (AD) analyses further showed that prediction performance was associated with both structural and kinetic response coverage of the training set. SHAP analysis identified substructures related to predicted chlorination reactivity and revealed that their SHAP contributions varied with their local bonding environments. Application to 642 river-basin contaminants prioritized seven primary candidates within the AD for subsequent investigation of DBP formation. These results demonstrate the utility of the substructure token-based pre-trained molecular representations for chlorination kinetics prediction under limited data. The framework also provides an interpretable approach for chlorination kinetics prediction and a practical strategy for the prioritization of candidates for subsequent DBP formation investigation.

new_candidate_reviews.title: Multiscale multimodal integration of spatial omics through a deep generative model with CORAL
new_candidate_reviews.abstract: Spatial omics enable the in situ characterization of tissue architecture by measuring molecular modalities. However, integrating these datasets remains challenging due to differences in spatial resolution, cross-modal alignment and molecular coverage. Here we show that Cross-scale spatial Omics Registration and Analysis via graph Learning (CORAL), a probabilistic deep generative model, leverages graph attention to integrate diverse spatial transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic and epigenomic data across spatial scales. Applied to spatial transcriptomic and proteomic data from hepatocellular carcinoma patients before and after immunotherapy, CORAL identified organized immune-cell subsets and signaling pathways associated with therapeutic resistance. These results demonstrate CORAL's broad applicability for resolving tissue organization and clinically relevant multicellular interactions.

new_candidate_reviews.title: Interlayer single-metal-atom coordinated porous boron nitride: Triggering p-d-p orbital hybridization for efficient electrocatalytic nitrate to ammonia reduction
new_candidate_reviews.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 RR) represents a sustainable paradigm for simultaneous environmental remediation and green NH 3 production. While single-atom catalysts (SACs) exhibit immense promise for NO 3 RR, precisely manipulating their localized orbital interactions to decode the underlying structure-activity relationships remains a critical challenge. Herein, using density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we designed a series of interlayer single-metal-atom coordinated porous boron nitride (IC-M/p-BN) acting as efficient electrocatalysts for NO 3 RR. Interlayer metal confinement triggers robust interfacial p-d-p orbital hybridization, establishing an efficient electron relay that empowers surface-exposed non-metallic B sites to act as direct catalytic centers while effectively suppressing the competing HER, NRR and toxic NO/NO 2 byproducts. Crucially, this interfacial charge transfer drives a dynamic B sp 2 -to-sp 3 reconfiguration, facilitating optimal NO 3 - activation. Benefiting from this mechanism, IC-Co/p-BN and IC-Ni/p-BN deliver outstanding NO 3 RR activity (limiting potentials of -0.51 and -0.50 V vs. RHE), significantly outperforming their conventional h-BN counterparts. Furthermore, machine learning analysis identifies the work function as the fundamental descriptor governing NO 3 - adsorption, revealing the interfacial catalytic mechanism. Our work not only offers a robust design strategy for high-efficiency 2D confined SACs but also provides deeper insights into the dynamic NO 3 - -to-NH 3 conversion mechanism at non-metallic interfaces.

new_candidate_reviews.title: Seasonal variations and influencing factors of daytime mercury oxidation in the urban atmosphere
new_candidate_reviews.abstract: Atmospheric mercury oxidation is crucial to global mercury cycling but remains poorly understood, particularly in the complex urban atmosphere. Here we identified the seasonal variations and influencing factors of daytime mercury oxidation in the urban atmosphere using one-year of dual-channel observations, machine learning and chemical box modelling. We found that the daytime increase in GOM/TGM ratio was most pronounced in summer (11.5 ± 5.5%) and weakest in winter (6.8 ± 3.8%). This seasonal variation in mercury oxidation intensity is regulated by distinct factors: oxidation-related species in summer, meteorological conditions in spring and autumn, and particle-related processes in winter. By analyzing the seasonal influence of oxidation-related species, we find that ozone primarily enhances mercury oxidation by promoting the formation of oxidizing radicals, and this promoting effect exhibits clear seasonal variability, leading to the strongest effect in summer and the weakest in winter. In contrast, based on box model results in differentiated scenarios, the NO 2 inhibits mercury oxidation mainly by reducing the availability of oxidizing radicals, and this inhibitory effect shows little seasonal variation. Incorporating the roles of O 3 and NO 2 on mercury oxidation through their seasonally varying regulation of radical availability can provide a more comprehensive understanding of atmospheric mercury oxidation and its cycling patterns.

new_candidate_reviews.title: Development and validation of early warning scores predicting 24 h mortality addressing intercurrent medical interventions in Denmark: a multicentre retrospective cohort study of 2·08 million hospital encounters
new_candidate_reviews.abstract: Background The National Early Warning Score (NEWS) is widely used to predict patient deterioration, but retrospective validations face intervention bias and emphasise discrimination performance over clinical utility. We aimed to compare the clinical net benefit of NEWS against simplified scoring rules and machine learning models, to determine whether simpler approaches suffice or if complex models offer meaningful advantages, and to evaluate performance heterogeneity across patient subgroups. Methods In this multicentre retrospective cohort study, we included data from 15 Danish hospitals (ten hospital networks) across the Capital and Zealand regions of Denmark, between Oct 16, 2018, and Oct 16, 2023. We included all adults (aged ≥18 years) with a hospital encounter with at least one NEWS assessment. Demographic and clinical data, NEWS data, and time of death were extracted from hospital and regional electronic health records. Patients were followed up until death or completion of the 24 h observation period after the initial NEWS score was recorded, whichever occurred first. The outcome was all-cause mortality within 24 h of the initial NEWS recording. We compared NEWS against both simpler and more complex approaches for predicting 24 h mortality: simplified NEWS (NEWS without blood pressure and temperature), Demographic Early Warning Score (DEWS; simplified NEWS with age and sex), and a model based on Extreme Gradient Boosting Early Warning Score (XGB-EWS) incorporating vital signs, demographics, laboratory markers, plus medical history embeddings extracted using sentence transformers. We used propensity score weighting to mitigate intervention bias and evaluated performance using net benefit, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, and calibration. Findings This study included data for 2 080 765 hospital encounters representing 825 200 unique patients over 5 years. The majority (50·9%) of the weighted population was aged 18-65 years, 50·4% were female, 49·6% were male, and 66·2% were admitted to internal and acute medicine clinical specialties. Decision curve analysis in the overall population showed maximum net benefit differences of 1·9 additional correct mortality identifications per 10 000 patients between XGB-EWS and NEWS, and 1·5 per 10 000 patients between NEWS and simplified NEWS. However, stratified analyses revealed substantial heterogeneity: in the high-risk group (initial NEWS ≥7), XGB-EWS provided a maximum gain of 78·1 correct identifications per 10 000 patients compared with NEWS, whereas simplified NEWS resulted in a maximum performance loss of 60·2 per 10 000 patients. Conversely, in the low-risk group (NEWS 0-4), differences were minimal: XGB-EWS provided a maximum gain of 0·9 correct identifications per 10 000 patients compared with NEWS, while simplified NEWS resulted in a maximum loss of 0·1 per 10 000 patients. Interpretation Model complexity produced small average clinical utility gains, concentrated among patients initially classified as high risk by NEWS. These findings support prospective trials of risk-stratified monitoring based on the first NEWS assessment, testing simplified approaches for lower-risk patients while retaining full NEWS or electronic health record models for higher-risk patients. Funding Novo Nordisk Foundation.

new_candidate_reviews.title: Integration and annotation of spatial multi-omic data with DIRAC
new_candidate_reviews.abstract: Spatial multi-omic technologies measure multiple molecular layers within intact tissues. Two central challenges are vertical integration, which combines different molecular modalities, and horizontal integration, which aligns cell types across studies. Here we show domain invariant representation through adaptive calibration (DIRAC), a geometric deep learning model that unifies these tasks in a generalized domain adaptation framework. DIRAC learns task-discriminative features that are insensitive to domain shifts caused by batch effects, omic modalities or study sites, enabling a shared embedding space and automated cell-type annotation through label transfer from reference datasets. Across sequencing-based and imaging-based datasets, DIRAC identified a new microvascular proliferation domain in glioblastoma, corrected cortical-layer annotations in severe Alzheimer's disease, resolved subtle structures in mouse embryos and remained robust to missing data and unseen cell types. We generated mouse spleen and thymus Stereo-CITE-seq data and used DIRAC to reveal thymic T cell migration and splenic immune cell interactions. DIRAC is fast and scales to millions of cells.

new_candidate_reviews.title: Plant sexual reproduction in a warming world
new_candidate_reviews.abstract: Sexual reproduction is the most heat-sensitive phase of the plant life cycle; however, studies of reproductive failure under heat stress have primarily focused on individual organs. Here, we propose a conceptual framework in which heat stress causes a system-level breakdown of male and female gametophyte development, shared metabolic and proteostatic support networks, and pollen-pistil interaction. This combined collapse within a narrow temperature window cannot be predicted from individual organs or gametophytes. Heat also remodels epigenetic makeup, generating stress memory, though its transmission across generations remains unresolved. We highlight that techniques such as single-cell omics, AI-driven phenotyping, and genome editing can provide valuable mechanistic insights to support the development of predictive, actionable breeding strategies for heat-resilient crops.

new_candidate_reviews.title: MambaSleepCVD for prediction of long term cardiovascular outcomes from polysomnography
new_candidate_reviews.abstract: Abstract Long-term cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk prediction remains a major global clinical priority. This study investigates how much prognostic information full-night polysomnography (PSG) carries after explicitly controlling demographic confounding, and whether combining specialized unimodal representations with continuous fusion mechanisms can effectively leverage it. We adopt a modular framework based on Coupled Mamba for simultaneous cross-modal and temporal fusion, capturing long-range dependencies and dynamic interactions between physiological modalities throughout sleep. With this capability, we assess whether specialized supervised representations from task-specific unimodal encoders offer prognostic value comparable to task-agnostic multimodal self-supervised pre-training. Validated on the Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS) dataset, our approach achieves performance comparable to or better than current state-of-the-art architectures in the fully supervised, data-abundant regime, although the cardiac channel alone accounts for most of the discriminative signal. More importantly, we show that in the reference dataset chronological age strongly drives survival ranking; when provided as an explicit input, it can create a shortcut that obscures the contribution of PSG-derived physiology. Ultimately, our findings suggest that supervised unimodal experts integrated through a fusion engine provide a flexible pathway for prognostic risk ranking from sleep recordings, while reliable CVD screening will require independent external cohorts and explicit confounder control.
